evidence: AC1: `npm test` exits 0 on Windows. `.milestoner/evidence/M01-test.txt` reports `# tests 82`, `# pass 82`, `# fail 0`, `# cancelled 0`, `# skipped 0`, with zero `not ok` lines. The pre-change baseline is kept beside it in `M01-test-baseline.txt`: `# pass 79`, `# fail 3` (three, not the six the prompt predicted, because the working tree was mixed: 75 files CRLF, 30 already LF).

AC2: NOT confirmed by CI, and this is the one gap. AC2 asks for a CI run id; protocol section 5 forbids `git push`, so no CI run exists for the closing commit 9d294d8, and there is no WSL on this host for a real Linux run. Evidenced locally instead: the suite passes against a working tree that is now byte-identical to a POSIX checkout (`git ls-files --eol -- ':!.milestoner'` reports `i/lf w/lf` for 99 of 100 files, the hundredth being empty), and every change is a verified no-op on LF input. `.milestoner/evidence/M01-posix-check.txt` shows `normalisation-is-identity=true` for all five files the touched tests read, and `pathToFileURL` producing `file:///D:/Dev/milestoner/src/state.ts`, the specifier form Node accepts on every platform and a strict widening of the bare path POSIX already accepted. Push and read the matrix to close this properly.

AC3: `.milestoner/evidence/M01-test.txt` line 91 reads `ok 15 - concurrent writers from separate processes do not lose an update`, against `not ok 15 ... every writer must exit cleanly, actual [1]` at the same line in the baseline. Exit codes captured directly in `.milestoner/evidence/M01-lock-writers.txt`: `platform: win32`, `writer exit codes: [0,0,0,0,0,0]`, `evidence entries surviving: 6 of 6`, `rev: 6`. D-022's cross-process locking guarantee is verified on Windows rather than skipped by an ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME load failure.

AC4: `.milestoner/evidence/M01-diffstat.txt` holds `git diff --stat 5d22e25 8207e59`: five files, `.gitattributes`, `scripts/gen-skill.mjs`, `src/lock.test.ts`, `src/plugin-commands.test.ts`, `src/templates/skill.test.ts`. Across both commits of the milestone, `git diff --name-only 5d22e25 HEAD -- src | grep -v '\.test\.ts$'` returns 0 lines and `git diff --stat 5d22e25 HEAD -- src` lists only the three `*.test.ts`. The second commit 9d294d8 is documentation and run files.

milestones.title: A registry of runs, and `milestoner runs`
evidence: AC1: `.milestoner/evidence/M02-runs.txt` sections 1 and 2 hold the real output of `milestoner runs` and `milestoner runs --json`, taken from a third directory that is not a milestoner project, while two runners started by `milestoner run` were live in two temp projects: `alive checkout-v2 M01 0/4 pid 40148 att 1` and `alive legacy-tests M01 0/3 pid 21408`, each with its own project path, and in JSON `runnerAlive: true`, `health: "alive"`, `lastEventSeconds: 6` for both. The producing script is beside it as `M02-demo.sh`. Covered by tests `ok 32 - two runs in different directories are both listed, each with its own milestone and verdict` and `ok 7 - both runs are printed with their project, milestone, progress and verdict` in `.milestoner/evidence/M02-test.txt`.

AC2: test `ok 33 - a runner that is gone leaves no live entry, and expires out of the file a day later`, which asserts `runnerAlive === false`, `health === "gone"`, then an empty listing and `pruned[0].reason === "expired"` past RETENTION_MS. Before/after live output in `M02-runs.txt`: section 1 prints `alive legacy-tests`, section 3 kills that runner's tree with `taskkill /F /T` so it never reaches its `finally`, and the same command then prints `gone legacy-tests M01 0/3 pid 21408` with `the runner is not running; relaunch it with milestoner run in that directory - last seen 9s ago` and `exit=2`. Also `ok 34 - a recycled pid is not mistaken for a live run`.

AC3: test `ok 36 - concurrent registration from several processes loses no entry` in `src/registry.test.ts`. Six separate node processes are spawned together and awaited together, each registering its own project root; the assertions are `[...new Set(codes)] === [0]` ("every runner must register cleanly") and that the listed run names equal all six ("every registration must survive"). Same D-022 argument as `lock.test.ts`: without the lock, six load-mutate-write cycles leave whoever renamed last holding a copy that never saw the other five. Serialisation is `withStateLock` itself, reused rather than reimplemented.

AC4: tests `ok 35 - a registered project whose directory is gone is pruned and reported, not fatal` (asserts the surviving run is still listed, `pruned.length === 1`, `reason === "project-gone"`, and that a second read reports nothing because the entry was dropped from the file) and `ok 9 - a deleted project is reported as pruned and does not take the listing down with it`. Live in `M02-runs.txt` section 4: after `rm -rf` of the checkout-api project the listing still prints the other run and adds `pruned checkout-v2 (...): its .milestoner directory is gone`; section 5 prints the registry file to show the entry is gone from it.

AC5: `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `## D-025 - A machine-level registry of runs, behind `milestoner runs` (2026-08-20)`, one paragraph per required decision. What is registered: live runners with a 24-hour retention window for a killed runner, against registering only live runners (a run that died at 2am has vanished by morning) and scanning the disk for `.milestoner` directories (finds runs nobody has touched in months, and turns a cheap question into a filesystem walk). Where the file lives: `~/.milestoner/runs.json`, `MILESTONER_HOME` overrides, XDG deliberately not honoured with the reason given, and best-effort writes when the home directory is not writable. How stale entries die: pid liveness corroborated by the project's own `pulse.json` naming that same pid and same run, with the residual case (killed runner, stale pulse, exact pid reuse) named and left to the retention window.

AC6: `docs/GUIDE.md` gained `### milestoner runs` between `### milestoner status` and `### milestoner unblock`: invocation, sample output, a verdict table (alive/slow/hung/unknown/gone/complete), the exit-code contract with the `notify-send` example, the registry file and `MILESTONER_HOME`, the pruning behaviour, and the note that there is still no panel across runs. Under `## Limits of v0.4` the item `**One run per project directory**, and no view across runs. There is no registry of the runs on a machine, so `serve` and `status` only ever show the directory they were started in.` is replaced by `**One run per project directory.** Runs across the machine are listed by [`milestoner runs`](#milestoner-runs), which reads a registry at `~/.milestoner/runs.json`, but there is still no *panel* across them`. `## The .milestoner directory` also names the one file outside the project.

Gate: `npm run typecheck` exit 0, `npm run build` exit 0, `npm test` exit 0. `.milestoner/evidence/M02-test.txt` reports `# tests 97`, `# pass 97`, `# fail 0`, `# cancelled 0`, `# skipped 0`, zero `not ok` lines, against the 82/82 baseline in `M02-test-baseline.txt`. `claude plugin validate .` passes. Committed as e2769da (engine) and 187f743 (docs), tagged `v05/M02`; `dist/` is left built and green.

milestones.title: `kill` ends the whole session on every platform
evidence: AC1: `.milestoner/evidence/M03-ci.txt` holds CI run id 32383755761 (https://github.com/fabrodz/milestoner/actions/runs/32383755761) on branch v05/M03 at sha 57850f5, event pull_request (#1), verdict success, with all eight job conclusions. The appended section quotes the job logs, fetched with `gh api repos/fabrodz/milestoner/actions/jobs/<id>/logs`: `ok 76 - a wrapper's grandchild is killed with the session, not orphaned`, `ok 77 - the runner's abort takes the grandchild with it too`, `ok 78 - a session that ignores SIGTERM is killed after the grace period`, in `ubuntu-latest / node 20` (job 96473048188, success) and `macos-latest / node 20` (job 96473048454, success), both closing at `# tests 100`, `# pass 100`, `# fail 0`. Test 76 in `src/session.kill.test.ts` spawns a wrapper that forks a grandchild, records the grandchild's pid to a file, writes a real `pulse.json` and kills through `kill()` itself, then asserts `isProcessAlive(grandchild) === false` with the message "the grandchild must not survive the kill".

AC2: `ok 58 - one interrupt lets the running session finish and be graded, then stops` and `ok 59 - a second interrupt kills the session and leaves the milestone in_progress`, both from `src/runner.stop.test.ts`. Passing locally in `.milestoner/evidence/M03-test.txt` and, which is what matters for a `detached` change, quoted from the ubuntu and macos job logs in `M03-ci.txt`.

AC3: local Windows suite `.milestoner/evidence/M03-test.txt` reports `# tests 100`, `# pass 100`, `# fail 0`, `# cancelled 0`, `# skipped 0`, with zero `not ok` lines, against the 97/97 baseline M02 left. CI `windows-latest / node 20` (job 96473048237) and `windows-latest / node 24` (job 96473048107) both `success`; tests 58, 59 and 76-78 are quoted from job 96473048237 in `M03-ci.txt`. Windows keeps `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`; the only Windows change is the runner's abort path adopting that same tree kill instead of ending the cmd shim alone.

AC4: `docs/DECISIONS.md` line 443, `## D-026 - The agent session gets its own process group, and the kill escalates (2026-08-20)`. A dedicated paragraph states what `detached` changes about Ctrl-C: the child leaves the terminal's foreground process group, so Ctrl-C in the terminal running `milestoner run` reaches the runner and nothing else, where the tty previously delivered SIGINT straight to the agent and usually killed it on the first press, which quietly broke the two-interrupt contract on POSIX. Rejected alternative recorded: walking the process table for children of the pid. Also covers the SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL-after-five-seconds escalation and why it is skipped on Windows.

Gate: `npm run typecheck` exit 0, `npm run build` exit 0, `npm test` exit 0, `claude plugin validate .` exit 0, `node --version` v22.20.0. Suite green on all three platforms in CI run 32383755761. Code landed as 57850f5, closed by 320a910, tagged `v05/M03`; `dist/` left built and green (`node dist/cli.js --version` prints 0.4.0).

milestones.title: The panel comes up with the run
evidence: AC1: test `ok 58 - the panel comes up with the run and answers with this run's live state` in `src/runner.serve.test.ts`, which fetches `/api/state` off the URL the run printed and asserts the pulse names this runner's pid and the milestone in flight, then that the run drained to `done`. The captured request and response are in `.milestoner/evidence/M04-serve.txt` section 1, taken against the built `dist/cli.js`: `milestoner run --serve --port 1640`, its banner, `GET /api/state?token=...` answering `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `"run": "panel-demo"`, M01 `in_progress`, `"runnerAlive": true`, `"agentAlive": true`, `"lastEvent": "session-launched"`, followed by `RUN COMPLETE` with M01 `done` and 1 evidence line.

AC2: test `ok 59 - the panel is closed once the run ends, and its port is free again`, which asserts `fetch(url)` rejects after `run()` resolves ("the panel must not answer once the run has ended") and that a fresh server can bind the same port ("the port must be free, not held by a stream nobody closed"). The panel is closed in the same `finally` as `clearPulse` and `deregisterRun` in `src/runner.ts`. End to end in `.milestoner/evidence/M04-serve.txt` section 2: after `runner exit code: 0`, `connection refused: ECONNREFUSED` and `port 1640 bindable again: yes`.

AC3: `src/runner.stop.test.ts` untouched and passing - `ok 63 - one interrupt lets the running session finish and be graded, then stops` and `ok 64 - a second interrupt kills the session and leaves the milestone in_progress`. With a panel attached: `ok 61 - one interrupt with a panel attached still finishes and grades the running session` (M01 `done` with `["AC1: ran to the end"]`, M02 still `pending`, panel closed) and `ok 62 - a second interrupt with a panel attached still leaves the milestone in_progress` (`attempts` 0, `history.length` 0, panel closed). The panel path installs no SIGINT or SIGTERM handler; `src/commands/serve.ts` is the only place those are bound.

AC4: test `ok 60 - a port already in use moves the panel and does not take the run down`, which squats a port, asserts the panel did not claim it, asserts the printed line `port <n> is already in use - the panel is on port `, and asserts the panel that did come up answers for this run and that M01 finished `done`. The exact message from the real CLI is in `.milestoner/evidence/M04-serve.txt` section 3: `port 4400 is already in use - the panel is on port 1557 instead`, then `runner exit code 0; M01 is done - the busy port cost the run nothing`.

AC5: `milestoner serve` is covered by `ok 67` through `ok 77` in `src/server/http.test.ts`, all unchanged and passing, including `ok 73 - a read-only panel refuses every write and says so in its state` and `ok 69 - a Host header we did not expect is refused before anything else happens`. Its observable output is captured against the built CLI in `.milestoner/evidence/M04-serve.txt` section 5: the read-only banner, the read-write banner with both warning lines and `Ctrl-C to stop`, and a busy port still giving `port 4400 is already in use - pick another with --port` with exit code 1. Flags and the read-only default are unchanged; `serve` now calls the extracted `startPanel` with `onBusy: "fail"`.

AC6: `docs/DECISIONS.md` gained `## D-027 - The panel comes up with the run, and what that costs (2026-08-20)`, one paragraph per decision: `--write` is allowed and `/api/run/start` is what goes (409, with the page reading a new `canStart` field), a busy port moves the attached panel while `serve` still fails, and `--open` is not offered because the URL is the credential. `README.md`: the `run` row of the command table carries `[--serve]`, and `## The web panel` now opens on both commands with a paragraph on the three differences and the absent `--open`. `docs/GUIDE.md`: new `#### Watching it in a browser: --serve` under `### milestoner run` with the difference table, cross-links from `### milestoner serve` and from quickstart step 6, and the `## Limits of v0.4` entry updated. `CHANGELOG.md` under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`.

Committed as 79ebdab (engine) and 8893961 (docs), tagged `v05/M04`; `dist/` left built and green (`node dist/cli.js --version` prints 0.4.0).

milestones.title: The state lock cannot be broken by the process that just took it
evidence: AC1 done: regression tests drive the empty-lock window deterministically. Pre-fix (src/lock.ts from cf4fa0c, one word `export` added, stated in the file): exit 1, pass 8 / fail 3, with `not ok 5 - an empty lock is a lock acquired this instant, and a contender must not break it`, `not ok 7 - a contender that meets an empty lock waits out the grace instead of stealing it` (waited 22ms), `not ok 8 - release removes only its own lock, never one that was broken and retaken`. Post-fix: exit 0, pass 11 / fail 0. Both runs captured in .milestoner/evidence/M05-lock.txt.

AC2 done: `concurrent registration from several processes loses no entry` and `concurrent writers from separate processes do not lose an update`, hardened to 24 and 30 interleaved acquisitions, ran 10 repeated rounds, every round exit 0 with pass 20 / fail 0 and zero `not ok` lines (.milestoner/evidence/M05-repeats.txt). Full suite 111/111 in .milestoner/evidence/M05-test.txt against the 106/106 baseline.

AC3 NOT achieved, and it is the blocker: CI run 32423986143 (wip/M05 at 9621f63, PR #3) - all eight jobs, the three ubuntu jobs included, `failure` with zero steps executed, annotation 'The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased', identically on the initial trigger and on `gh run rerun`. AC4 done: docs/DECISIONS.md, `D-028 - The lock carries its holder from the first instant, because D-022 broke empty locks on sight (2026-08-20)`. Opens on what D-022 got wrong, then one paragraph per required decision (linkSync publication and the no-hard-links fallback, the mtime-keyed 3s grace for unreadable locks, the steal-and-run-unlocked fallback removed with an ownership-checked release), each with the rejected alternative.
AC5 done: CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] / Fixed, first line: 'Two milestoner processes writing state at the same moment could silently lose one of the writes'.

Gate: npm run typecheck exit 0, npm run build exit 0, npm test exit 0 (111/111), claude plugin validate . exit 0. milestones.title: A crashed agent does not cost the milestone an attempt
evidence: AC1: test `ok 95 - an agent that crashed after fifteen minutes of work does not cost the milestone an attempt` in .milestoner/evidence/M06-test.txt, fed the M03 shape verbatim (929 seconds, 15 bytes, text `Execution error`, wroteResult false); asserts reason `crash`, waitSeconds = infra.genericWaitSeconds, and a detail naming `929s` and `15-byte`. Exit code is absent from InfraInput by design - the verdict never comes from it - stated in the test comment.

AC2: every pre-existing classification test passes unchanged in M06-test.txt: `ok 90` instant death, `ok 91`/`ok 92`/`ok 99` usage limits and reset parsing, `ok 98` infraFailurePatterns, `ok 93` wroteResult wins, and the charged cases `ok 94` (120 B at 4000 s stays null) and `ok 100` (full transcript, never refunded). Suite `# tests 114`, `# pass 114`, `# fail 0` against the 111/111 baseline in M06-test-baseline.txt, zero `not ok` lines.

AC3: boundary tested from both sides, reading the threshold from the config key: `ok 96 - one byte under the crash line is a crash, however long the session ran` (99 B at 4000 s -> crash) and `ok 97 - at the crash line the transcript counts as work and the attempt is charged` (100 B at 4000 s -> null). Both in M06-test.txt.

AC4: docs/DECISIONS.md, `## D-029 - A transcript with nothing in it is a crash at any duration (2026-08-20)`, one paragraph per decision: the second lower threshold `infra.crashTranscriptBytes` (100 B) rather than a dropped bound, no refund above the line (a real transcript with no result stays incomplete and charged), and `infra.maxRetries` as the over-refund ceiling, each with its rejected alternative.

AC5: the `## Limits of v0.5` bullet `**A crashed session can still cost an attempt.**` is removed from docs/GUIDE.md, whose infrastructure-failures section now lists the crash rule as shape 3 with its any-duration wording; CHANGELOG.md carries it under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`, first line `A session that crashed mid-run no longer costs the milestone an attempt.` Committed as 090bf68, code as 2f07a42, tagged v05-debt-M06.
